pairs.question: Mene talem factum esse ut saepe fallar?
pairs.answer: At jam scio me in iis, quae perspicue intelligo, falli non posse.
pairs.derivation: Authorial self-objection posed as a question (the objection: that I was so made as to be often deceived) and immediately answered by Descartes himself with the refutation beginning 'At jam scio'. Window ends at the first full stop; the next sentence introduces a new objection ('Mene multa aliàs...'). No scaffolding present in either span.

pairs.question: Mene multa aliàs pro veris & certis habuisse, quae postea falsa esse deprehendi?
pairs.answer: Atqui nulla ex iis clare & distincte perceperam, sed hujus regulae veritatis ignarus ob alias causas forte credideram, quas postea minus firmas esse detexi.
pairs.derivation: Second authorial self-objection as interrogative, answered by Descartes with 'Atqui nulla ex iis...'. The answer runs to its full stop, ending before the next question 'Quid ergo dicetur?'. No scaffolding present.

pairs.question: Anne (ut nuper mihi objiciebam) me forte somniare, sive illa omnia, quae jam cogito, non magis vera esse quàm ea quae dormienti occurrunt?
pairs.answer: Imò etiam hoc nihil mutat; nam certe, quamvis somniarem, si quid intellectui meo sit evidens, illud omnino est verum.
pairs.derivation: Third authorial self-objection as interrogative (the dreaming doubt), introduced by 'Quid ergo dicetur?' and answered by 'Imò etiam hoc nihil mutat...'. The parenthetical '(ut nuper mihi objiciebam)' is the author's own words and is the interrogative's content, kept.
